definitions.explanation: The surface or shape exposed when an object is cut through, or a diagram showing such a view. Used in technical, scientific, and everyday contexts.

examples.japanese: ケーキの{断面|だんめん}がきれいだ。
examples.english: The cross-section of the cake is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {断面|だんめん}{図|ず}を{見|み}てください。
examples.english: Please look at the cross-sectional diagram.

examples.japanese: この{木|き}の{断面|だんめん}には{年輪|ねんりん}がはっきりと{見|み}える。
examples.english: The tree rings are clearly visible in this tree's cross-section.

notes:
Compound of {断|だん} (cut) + {面|めん} (surface). Refers to the surface revealed when something is sliced through. Used both technically (engineering, science) and colloquially (food photography, where showing a beautiful cross-section is popular on social media — often called {萌|も}え{断|だん}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {断面|だんめん}{図|ず}: cross-sectional diagram
- {断面|だんめん}{積|せき}: cross-sectional area
- {断面|だんめん}を{見|み}せる: to show the cross-section
- {萌|も}え{断|だん}: visually appealing cross-section (of food, slang)

RELATED WORDS:
- {断層|だんそう}: geological fault; stratum
- {側面|そくめん}: side view, lateral surface
- {表面|ひょうめん}: surface (outer)
